title: Weeping Higan Cherry: Shidarezakura You Can Visit
meta_description: Half of these stand in for a more famous predecessor, and Kyoto does not mind. Four weeping cherries mapped in Kyoto and Nara.
intro: Half of these are stand-ins for a more famous tree, and in Kyoto nobody minds. The weeping cherry everyone photographs at Maruyama Park is the second one on the spot, the original having gone. The Taiko cherry at Daigo-ji is not the tree Toyotomi Hideyoshi saw when he staged his enormous blossom party there in the spring of 1598, months before his death, but it stands where the party happened. Shidarezakura hang their flowering branches straight down, so the tree makes a curtain you walk under rather than a canopy you look up into, and they open before the ordinary somei-yoshino. Nara's is the extreme case: the weeping cherry beside the approach to Himuro Shrine opens before any other cherry in the city, and the local spring is dated from it. The fourth came out of the Kyoto Imperial Palace grounds as a gift, in the reign of Emperor Komei.
